method_card.title: Transport and Getting Around
method_card.content:
This lesson covers transport modes, prepositions of travel, comparisons between transport types, and how to describe journeys. The prescribed speaking setting for transport is the train station.

FrenchEnglish
en voitureby car
en trainby train
en busby bus
en avionby plane
en métroby underground
à véloby bike
à piedon foot
à motoby motorbike
un billet (aller simple)a (single) ticket
un billet aller-retoura return ticket
le quaithe platform
le départthe departure
l'arrivée (f)the arrival
rapidefast
pratiqueconvenient / practical
écologiqueeco-friendly

Grammar focus — prepositions with transport: Use en with enclosed vehicles: en voiture, en train, en bus, en avion, en métro. Use à with non-enclosed modes: à vélo, à pied, à moto. These prepositions do not change — they never use an article after them.

Comparatives for transport: plus rapide que (faster than), moins cher que (cheaper than), plus écologique que (more eco-friendly than). Example: Le train est moins cher que l'avion mais plus lent que la voiture. (The train is cheaper than the plane but slower than the car.)

Model paragraph: Pour aller au collège, je prends le bus parce que c'est pratique. Le week-end, j'aime aller à vélo parce que c'est écologique et bon pour la santé. Pour les longs voyages, je préfère le train parce que c'est moins cher que l'avion.
steps: Learn the transport modes with en (enclosed) and à (non-enclosed) prepositions
Use comparatives plus/moins + adjective + que to compare different transport types
Describe how you travel to different places and give a reason using parce que
Practise a train station role-play buying a ticket and asking for platform information

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — transport appears in all four skills papers

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Je préfère voyager en train parce que c'est moins cher que l'avion.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break it down: Je préfère voyager | en train | parce que | c'est moins cher que l'avion.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Je préfère voyager = I prefer to travel. en train = by train (use en for enclosed transport).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: moins cher que = cheaper than / less expensive than. l'avion = the plane.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I prefer to travel by train because it is cheaper than the plane.

worked_examples.question: How do you choose between en and à with transport?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Use en with enclosed vehicles where you sit inside: en voiture, en train, en bus, en avion, en métro, en bateau.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Use à with non-enclosed modes where you are exposed: à vélo, à pied, à moto, à cheval.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Neither takes an article after it: en voiture (not en la voiture), à vélo (not au vélo).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: en + enclosed vehicle (voiture, train, bus, avion, métro). à + non-enclosed mode (vélo, pied, moto). No article after either preposition.

bronze.question: Match the French transport vocabulary to the English meaning
Match the French travel words to the English meaning
Complete the sentences about transport with the correct preposition
sentence_parts: voiture parce que c'est rapide. Je préfère aller
vélo parce que c'est bon pour la santé. Le bus est moins

gaps.correct_explain: en voiture = by car. Use en before enclosed vehicles.

wrong.à: à voiture is incorrect. Use en with enclosed transport (voiture, train, bus, avion).
wrong.par: par voiture is not a standard French expression for transport. Use en.

gaps.correct_explain: à vélo = by bike. Use à with non-enclosed modes.

wrong.en: en vélo is incorrect. Use à with non-enclosed modes (vélo, pied, moto).

gaps.correct_explain: moins cher que = cheaper than. Le bus is masculine, so the adjective is cher.

wrong.chère: chère is feminine. Le bus is masculine, so you need cher.
wrong.rapide: rapide means fast — the sentence is about cost. Use cher.

bronze.question: Complete the comparison between transport types

gaps.correct_explain: moins rapide que = less fast than / slower than.

wrong.plus: plus rapide = faster than — but the train is slower than the car.

wrong.de: de is not used for comparisons. Use que.

gaps.correct_explain: moins cher que = cheaper than (less expensive than).

wrong.plus: plus cher = more expensive — the train is cheaper than the plane.

bronze.question: What does 'Pour aller en ville, je prends le bus parce que c'est pratique' mean?
options: To go into town, I take the bus because it is convenient.
To go into town, I take the train because it is fast.
I like going into town by bike because it is eco-friendly.
To go into town, I drive because it is practical.

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'The bike is more eco-friendly than the car'?
options: Le vélo est plus écologique que la voiture.
Le vélo est moins écologique que la voiture.
La voiture est plus écologique que le vélo.
Le vélo est aussi écologique que la voiture.

bronze.source_text: Je préfère aller à vélo parce que c'est écologique et bon pour la santé.
model_answers: I prefer to go by bike because it is eco-friendly and good for health.
I prefer cycling because it is eco-friendly and good for your health.
hints: aller à vélo = to go by bike
bon pour la santé = good for health

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
sentence_parts: Je voudrais un billet aller-retour pour Paris, s'il vous plaît. Le train
à quelle heure ? Il part du

gaps.correct_explain: part is the il form of partir (to leave/depart): il part.

wrong.pars: pars is the je/tu form. Le train is third person singular, so you need part.
wrong.partir: partir is the infinitive. After le train, conjugate: part.

gaps.correct_explain: le quai = the platform. Trains depart from a quai at a station.

wrong.gare: la gare = the station itself. The departure platform is le quai.

silver.english: I would like a return ticket to Paris, please. What time does the train leave? It leaves from platform five.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: L'avion est plus vite que le train.
silver.explanation: Vite is an adverb (quickly/fast), not an adjective. In comparisons with plus/moins/aussi, use the adjective rapide: L'avion est plus rapide que le train.
silver.translation: The plane is faster than the train.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: I prefer to travel by train because it is less expensive than the plane.

distractor_labels.à: wrong preposition — train is an enclosed vehicle, needs en not à

silver.source_text: I go to school by bus but at the weekend I like to go by bike because it is more eco-friendly.
model_answers: Je vais au collège en bus mais le week-end j'aime aller à vélo parce que c'est plus écologique.
Je vais au lycée en bus mais le week-end j'aime aller à vélo parce que c'est plus écologique.
hints: to school = au collège / au lycée

gold.source_text: Last year, I travelled to Paris by train with my family. The journey took two hours and it was very comfortable. In the future, I would like to travel by plane because it is faster, but it is less eco-friendly.
model_answers: L'année dernière, j'ai voyagé à Paris en train avec ma famille. Le voyage a duré deux heures et c'était très confortable. À l'avenir, je voudrais voyager en avion parce que c'est plus rapide, mais c'est moins écologique.

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a train station in France. You want to travel to Lyon. You approach the ticket office.

bullets.prompt: Greet the ticket officer and ask for a return ticket to Lyon.
bullets.model_answer: Bonjour ! Je voudrais un billet aller-retour pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît.
bullets.note: greeting + je voudrais + un billet aller-retour + pour + city

bullets.prompt: Ask what time the next train leaves and which platform it goes from.
bullets.model_answer: À quelle heure part le prochain train ? Et il part de quel quai ?
bullets.note: question with inversion: part le prochain train + quel quai (platform)

bullets.prompt: Say the journey will take about two hours and ask if there is a restaurant carriage.
bullets.model_answer: Le voyage durera environ deux heures. Est-ce qu'il y a un wagon-restaurant dans le train ?
bullets.note: future tense: durera + environ (about) + il y a + wagon-restaurant

bullets.prompt: Thank the officer and say you will travel by train more often in the future because it is eco-friendly.
bullets.model_answer: Merci beaucoup ! À l'avenir, je prendrai le train plus souvent parce que c'est écologique.
bullets.note: merci + future tense: je prendrai (prendre irregular) + plus souvent + parce que

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: L'année dernière, j'ai voyagé en train et c'était très confortable. À l'avenir, je voudrais aller à vélo plus souvent parce que c'est plus écologique.
gold.correct_text: L'année dernière, j'ai voyagé en train et c'était très confortable. À l'avenir, je voudrais aller à vélo plus souvent parce que c'est plus écologique.
gold.translation: Last year, I travelled by train and it was very comfortable. In the future, I would like to go by bike more often because it is more eco-friendly.

gold.question: Complete the sentence (Higher grammar — si clause)
sentence_parts: les transports en commun, il y

gaps.correct_explain: utilisait is the imperfect of utiliser. In a si hypothetical clause, use the imperfect: Si + imparfait, + conditionnel.

wrong.utilise: utilise is the present tense. In a hypothetical si clause, use the imperfect: utilisait.
wrong.utilisera: utilisera is the future. Never use the future after si in a hypothetical clause — use the imperfect.

gaps.correct_explain: il y aurait = there would be. The conditional of il y a: irregular stem aur- + -ait.

wrong.aura: il y aura is the future. The result of a si + imperfect clause must be in the conditional: aurait.
wrong.a: il y a is the present. Use the conditional aurait for the result of a hypothetical.
